description: A stiff maize flour porridge that is the staple food of Kenya, served with vegetables, meat or fish.

steps.instruction: Bring 4 cups of water to a boil in a heavy pot. Add a pinch of salt.
Gradually add maize flour while stirring continuously with a wooden spoon to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat to low. Continue stirring and folding the ugali for 8–10 minutes until it pulls away from the sides of the pot and forms a firm, smooth ball.
Shape into a mound using a wet spoon. Serve hot on a plate alongside sukuma wiki, beans, or stew.

serving_suggestion: Serve with sukuma wiki, beans stew, or any meat dish.

description: Fragrant spiced rice cooked with beef and pilau masala, a celebratory dish popular across Kenya.

steps.instruction: Wash rice and soak for 10 minutes. Drain and set aside. Brown beef cubes in oil for 5–7 minutes.
Add sliced onion and cook until golden. Add minced garlic and pilau masala, stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped tomatoes (if using) and cook until softened. Add drained rice and stir to coat with spices.
Pour in water and add salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 20–25 minutes until rice is tender and liquid absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot with kachumbari.

serving_suggestion: Serve with kachumbari (tomato-onion salad) or a side of greens.

description: Soft, layered flatbreads made from wheat flour, a beloved accompaniment to stews and tea in Kenyan homes.

steps.instruction: Mix flour and salt. Add water gradually and knead into a soft, smooth dough.
Divide dough into 6–8 balls. Cover and let rest for 30 minutes.
Roll each ball into a thin circle. Brush with oil, fold into a spiral, and roll out again gently.
Cook on a hot dry pan for 2–3 minutes per side, brushing with oil, until golden spots appear.

serving_suggestion: Serve with beef stew, goat stew, or beans.

description: Tender boiled cassava roots, a simple and filling snack or side dish enjoyed across Kenya.

steps.instruction: Peel cassava, remove the central woody pith, and cut into serving-sized pieces. Wash well.
Place in a pot, cover with water, and add salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 25–30 minutes until cassava is fork-tender.
Drain and serve warm, optionally with tea or a dipping sauce.

serving_suggestion: Serve with hot tea or as a side to stew.

description: Steamed arrowroot pieces with a naturally earthy flavour, a traditional Kenyan side or snack.

steps.instruction: Peel arrowroot and cut into chunks. Wash under running water.
Place in a pot with water and salt. Bring to a boil.
Simmer for 20–25 minutes until tender when pierced with a fork.
Drain and serve hot as a snack or side dish.

serving_suggestion: Serve with tea or alongside a meat stew.

description: Charred roasted maize on the cob, a ubiquitous Kenyan street snack seasoned with salt, lemon or chilli.

steps.instruction: Husk fresh maize cobs and remove silk.
Roast over hot charcoal or on a grill, turning frequently, for 10–15 minutes until kernels are charred in spots.
Sprinkle with salt and optionally squeeze lemon juice or dust with chilli powder. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Enjoy as a street-style snack on its own.

name_sw: Nyama ya Ng'ombe ya Wet Fry
description: Tender beef simmered in a rich tomato-onion sauce, a popular Kenyan restaurant and home dish.

steps.instruction: Cut beef into cubes. Boil with salt and a little water until tender, about 30 minutes. Reserve broth.
Heat oil in a pan. Sauté onions until golden, then add garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a thick sauce.
Add boiled beef and stir to coat. Add reserved broth and simmer for 10–15 minutes until sauce thickens.
Adjust salt and serve hot with ugali or rice.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali, chapati, or steamed rice.

description: Slow-cooked goat meat in a spiced tomato gravy until fall-off-the-bone tender, a dish for special occasions.

steps.instruction: Brown goat meat in hot oil for 8–10 minutes in a heavy pot.
Add chopped onions and cook until golden. Stir in garlic, ginger, and spices.
Add grated tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add water, cover tightly, and simmer on low heat for 1 to 1.5 hours until meat is very tender.
Adjust salt, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali, rice, or chapati and kachumbari.

description: Chicken pieces simmered in a savory tomato and onion base, a comforting everyday Kenyan meal.

steps.instruction: Boil chicken pieces with salt and water until tender, about 25–30 minutes. Reserve broth.
In another pot, heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until softened and saucy.
Add boiled chicken and reserved broth. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until flavors meld.
Serve hot with ugali, rice, or chapati.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and sukuma wiki.

description: Beef liver pan-fried with onions and tomatoes, a quick and nutritious Kenyan favorite.

steps.instruction: Slice liver into thin strips and rinse. Pat dry.
Heat oil and sauté onions until softened. Add garlic if using.
Add liver and cook on high heat for 3–4 minutes until browned.
Add chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook for 5–7 minutes until tomatoes break down and liver is cooked through.
Serve hot with ugali or rice.

description: Boiled beef tripe stir-fried with onions, tomatoes, and spices, a hearty Kenyan delicacy.

steps.instruction: Clean tripe thoroughly. Boil in salted water for 1 to 1.5 hours until very tender. Cut into strips.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic, ginger, and curry powder if using.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until softened.
Add boiled tripe and stir-fry for 5–10 minutes until well coated and heated through.
Adjust salt and serve hot.

description: Minced beef cooked with onions and tomatoes into a rich, savory stew, often served with rice or ugali.

steps.instruction: Heat oil and sauté onions until soft. Add garlic if using.
Add minced beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Add chopped tomatoes and salt. Cook for 10 minutes until tomatoes break down.
Add water and simmer for 5–10 minutes until sauce thickens. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice, ugali, or chapati.

description: Hearty beef ribs slow-cooked in a flavorful tomato and onion gravy until tender.

steps.instruction: Boil beef ribs in salted water for 45–60 minutes until tender. Reserve broth.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and ginger.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until thick.
Add boiled ribs and reserved broth. Simmer for 20–30 minutes until sauce coats the ribs.
Adjust salt and serve hot.

description: Whole tilapia fried until crispy and often served with a side of ugali and greens.

steps.instruction: Clean and scale tilapia. Score the sides and rub with salt and lemon juice.
Heat oil in a deep pan until hot but not smoking.
Fry fish for 5–7 minutes per side until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with ugali and sukuma wiki.

description: Small dried sardines cooked in a rich onion and tomato sauce, a classic dish from the Lake Victoria region.

steps.instruction: Rinse omena well and drain. Optionally dry-fry in a pan for 2 minutes to remove excess moisture.
Heat oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic if using.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until softened.
Add omena and stir. Cook for 5–7 minutes until well mixed and heated through. Adjust salt.
Serve hot with ugali.

description: Dried dagaa (silver cyprinid) simmered in a tomato-based sauce, a nutritious lakeside staple.

steps.instruction: Rinse dagaa and set aside.
Sauté onions in oil until soft. Add chopped tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add dagaa and water. Simmer for 5–7 minutes until flavors combine.
Adjust salt and serve hot with ugali or rice.

description: Firm Nile perch fillets fried until golden, a popular fish dish from Lake Victoria.

steps.instruction: Cut Nile perch into fillets or chunks. Rub with salt and lemon juice.
Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Fry fish for 4–5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with ugali or rice.

description: Tender beans simmered in a rich tomato and onion sauce, a protein-packed Kenyan staple.

steps.instruction: Soak beans overnight or boil for 5 minutes and let sit for 1 hour. Drain.
Boil beans in fresh water for 45–60 minutes until tender. Reserve liquid.
In another pot, sauté onions in oil until golden. Add garlic and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add cooked beans and some reserved liquid. Simmer for 10–15 minutes.
Add salt to taste and serve hot with ugali or rice.

description: Green grams (mung beans) cooked into a soft, flavorful stew with tomatoes and onions.

steps.instruction: Rinse green grams and boil in water for 30–40 minutes until soft.
In a separate pan, sauté onions until golden. Add garlic and tomatoes, cook until soft.
Add cooked green grams with some of their liquid. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Season with salt and serve hot with rice or ugali.

description: Pigeon peas stewed with coconut milk and spices, a coastal Kenyan favorite.

steps.instruction: Boil pigeon peas in water for 40–50 minutes until tender.
Sauté onions in oil until soft. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add cooked pigeon peas and coconut milk. Simmer for 10–15 minutes.
Season with salt and serve with rice or chapati.

description: A rich, nutty stew made with groundnuts, tomatoes, and onions, often served with rice or ugali.

steps.instruction: Roast groundnuts lightly, then grind into a paste or powder.
Sauté onions in oil until golden. Add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add groundnut paste and water. Stir well and simmer for 15–20 minutes until thickened.
Season with salt and serve hot with rice or ugali.

description: Kidney beans slow-cooked in a savory tomato sauce, a hearty and nutritious Kenyan meal.

steps.instruction: Soak kidney beans overnight. Drain and boil in fresh water for 45–60 minutes until tender.
Sauté onions in oil until golden. Add garlic and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add cooked beans and a little reserved liquid. Simmer for 10–15 minutes.
Add salt to taste and serve with ugali or rice.

description: Red lentils cooked into a thick, comforting stew with onions, tomatoes, and mild spices.

steps.instruction: Rinse lentils. Sauté onions in oil until soft. Add garlic and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add lentils and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20–25 minutes until lentils are soft and stew is thick.
Season with salt and serve hot with rice or chapati.

description: Crispy battered onion rings, a popular snack or side dish in Kenyan eateries.

steps.instruction: Slice onions into thick rings and separate them.
Make a batter with flour, egg (if using), salt, and water until smooth.
Dip onion rings in batter and fry in hot oil until golden brown, about 2–3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot as a snack.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a snack or side with kachumbari.

description: A fresh, zesty salad of tomatoes, onions, and coriander, the classic Kenyan condiment.

steps.instruction: Chop tomatoes and onion into small pieces. Finely chop fresh coriander.
Combine in a bowl. Squeeze lemon juice over and sprinkle with salt.
Toss gently and serve fresh alongside pilau, nyama choma, or any main dish.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a side with pilau, grilled meat, or rice.
